top_stories.title: Tesla Full Self-Driving v15 Release
points: Tesla released FSD v15, targeting biggest weaknesses: sign detection, pothole handling, school zone speed recognition, and speed camera awareness.
New vision encoder trained on millions of internet videos improves detection of signs, potholes, animals, and speed cameras.
Critical intervention rate is reduced 25-fold compared to the previous version.
New Reality View feature shows FSD's planned driving behavior in real-time for transparency; adds Bike Rack Mode for specific parking scenarios.
System remains supervised, requiring human monitoring at all times.

items.title: Anthropic AI-Assisted Proof of Riemann Hypothesis
points: An Anthropic researcher claims AI assistance helped produce a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, a 167-year-old math conjecture about the distribution of prime numbers.
The proof reportedly passed verification by proof-checking software.

items.title: Developer 'Vibe-Codes' an Inference Chip
points: A developer used AI to 'vibe-code' (build software by conversationally prompting AI rather than manually writing code) an FPGA (field-programmable gate array, a reprogrammable computer chip) to run a large language model.
This demonstrates new possibilities when AI handles complex technical/hardware domains.

items.title: Neuralink Expands Clinical Trials Amid Long-Term Questions
points: Neuralink increased its surgery rate and extended trials from the US to Canada and the UK.
Early participants now mentor new enrollees via video calls on adjusting to brain-implant technology.
Trial contracts currently lack upgrade provisions—participants must revert to pre-implant status if Neuralink doesn't commercialize a consumer product, creating uncertainty for early adopters.

items.title: AI's Role in Biology Has Fundamental Data Limits
points: AI effectiveness in biology depends not just on data volume but on what gets measured and data quality.
Systematically incomplete measurements risk preventing comprehensive understanding of complex biological systems like whole cells or tissues.
AI will become a powerful biology tool, but no clear path yet exists to fully document how complete cellular or tissue systems work.

items.title: China Dominates AI Video Production
points: More than 95% of new micro dramas released in China now use AI generation rather than traditional production.
AI video and voice quality improvements are expected to significantly impact the media industry by 2027.

items.title: Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Mini Runs Advanced AI on MacBook Pro
points: Inkling 2 Mini runs on a MacBook Pro with 32GB RAM, achieving 4x faster speeds at 1/6 the cost of comparable models.
Costs $0.15/$0.50 per 1M input/output tokens.
Uses 'token recycling'—passing each token through middle layers three times for deeper reasoning with fewer generated tokens—to match much larger model performance on consumer hardware.

items.title: Prediction: Single Agent Platform Replaces App Layer by 2027
points: A tech founder predicts one unified agent platform will replace the entire app layer by 2027, orchestrating all app logic via sandboxed runtimes and shared filesystems.
Every other piece of software becomes a data source for AI swarms (groups of coordinating AI agents).
Infrastructure stays simple, relying on markdown files and event sourcing (recording state changes as a sequence of events) rather than complex distributed systems.

items.title: AI Agents Transform Consumer Shopping and Liability
points: AI shopping agents on Stripe's Link Agent Wallet saw daily spending jump 80-fold since September and double in the past month.
Travel makes up over 40% of transactions, with more than 50% of customers returning frequently.
Starting November 24, Wells Fargo holds customers financially liable for their AI agents' actions, pushing developers toward strict permission controls and revocation mechanisms.

items.title: Meta AI Chief Warns Superintelligence Imminent; Stanford Study on AI Incidents
points: Meta's AI chief argues superintelligence (AI surpassing human capability across virtually all domains) is arriving within a year and humanity must prepare immediately.
A Stanford researcher finds most major AI incidents stem from agents hitting messy codebases or missing context rather than from attackers—preventable through better code audits and documentation.

items.title: Knowledge Factories: Applying Software Factory Principles to Knowledge Work
points: LangChain CEO Harrison Chase argues 'knowledge factories' require three components: documented skills (unwritten employee processes), domain knowledge (product/customer facts), and data access (how to query tools like Snowflake).
Implementation starts by identifying where agents get stuck on repetitive tasks, then systematically capturing missing knowledge with agent-suggested fixes.
A dedicated 'curator agent' should extract knowledge from Slack, Notion, and agent error traces, updating a knowledge base while keeping working agents isolated from edits to prevent contradictions.

items.title: US and Chinese Open-Weight AI Models Mutually Dependent
points: US and Chinese open-weight AI models (models with publicly released internal parameters) depend on each other more than expected.
Each ecosystem improves by learning from the other's architectural and training innovations, creating mutual competition that benefits both.

items.title: Jensen Huang Reinstated as Nvidia CEO
points: Nvidia's board voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as president, CEO, and board member effective immediately after a weeks-long foreign intelligence investigation.
Government officials were consulted and confirmed no national security risk from Huang's return.
An independent director committee will continue investigating reported foreign intelligence targeting of Huang.
A new national security committee will oversee trade compliance, and the company is hiring a chief compliance officer.

items.title: OpenAI Proposes Shared AI Training Safety Limits
points: OpenAI's chief scientist Jakub Pachocki published internal log-perplexity scores (a measure of how well a model predicts the next word) showing GPT-3.5 at 0.99 and GPT-4 at 0.91.
Pachocki proposed developers avoid crossing perplexity-based thresholds until safety oversight research hits clear milestones, like new chain-of-thought monitoring systems.
He requested joint adoption of evaluation standards, red-teaming protocols (systematic testing to find vulnerabilities), and transparency requirements across all AI labs.
Warning that safety research could lag behind training speed increases expected as early as 2027.

items.title: CrowdStrike Acquires Zscaler for $43.9 Billion
points: All-stock deal values Zscaler at $43.9 billion, paying shareholders 1.135 CrowdStrike shares per share (a 34% premium).
Combined entity projects $1 billion in additional yearly revenue and $500 million in cost savings.
Zscaler founder Jay Chaudhry continues leading the Zscaler business unit and joins CrowdStrike's board; Zscaler shareholders will own 15.9% of the combined company.
Deal expected to close in the second half of fiscal 2028, expanding CrowdStrike into cloud network protection.

items.title: US Intelligence Warns of Frequent Tech Outages
points: US intelligence warns Americans to expect frequent tech outages as systems upgrade infrastructure for the AI era.
